text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Work-up of the liver mass: multiphase contrast CT of the liver with CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis; MRI of the liver with MRCP if CT does not settle the origin; alpha-fetoprotein, CA 19-9 and CEA; hepatitis B surface antigen, core antibody and surface antibody, and hepatitis C antibody; liver function with Child-Pugh and ALBI scoring; and image-guided core biopsy, because a mass in a liver without cirrhosis cannot be diagnosed by imaging alone
  • Medical oncology consultation for a solid liver mass with weight loss: diagnosis, staging, multidisciplinary tumor board review, and treatment
  • Symptom care during the work-up: acetaminophen up to 3,000 mg a day, small frequent meals with a dietitian's advice, weight at every visit, and a same-day call for jaundice, fever, vomiting, dark urine or worse pain; results shared with him in full as they arrive, by one coordinating clinician
  • Staging laparoscopy before any attempt at resection, with biopsy of any peritoneal disease and an implanted port under the same anesthetic; if no metastases, extended cholecystectomy with resection of liver segments IVb and V and portal lymphadenectomy; comprehensive genomic profiling of the biopsy tissue (HER2, mismatch repair and microsatellite status, BRAF, FGFR2, IDH1, NTRK, RET, KRAS, tumor mutational burden)
  • Hepatitis B reactivation monitoring for resolved infection (surface antigen negative, core antibody positive, HBV DNA undetectable): HBV DNA and ALT every 3 months during treatment and for at least 6 to 12 months after, with entecavir started promptly if HBV DNA becomes detectable or surface antigen reappears
  • First-line systemic therapy for stage IVB gallbladder adenocarcinoma: gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 and cisplatin 25 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8 with durvalumab 1,500 mg on day 1 every 21 days for up to 8 cycles, then durvalumab 1,500 mg every 4 weeks until progression or unacceptable toxicity; blood count, creatinine, magnesium and liver tests before each dose; TSH every cycle; CA 19-9 each cycle; CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis every 2 to 3 months; teaching on immune-related side effects; ondansetron at home
  • Specialist palliative care alongside cancer treatment from the diagnosis of advanced disease: symptoms, nutrition, coping, goals of care, a health care agent, and a family meeting if and when he chooses
  • Magnesium oxide 400 mg by mouth daily for cisplatin-related low magnesium, rechecked with each dose; durvalumab maintenance every 4 weeks after the eighth cycle, with restaging CT every 2 to 3 months
